hero.title: Web Developer
hero.intro: Frontend developer with 5 years of experience, I turn complex requirements into simple, intuitive interfaces.

iris.name: Iris
iris.description: The web application hosting Egis' internal AI product, deployed to 18,000 employees with 5,000 daily active users. Designed and developed features end-to-end.
highlights: Chat, leaderboard and gamification systems shipped end-to-end
Custom logo-based loading screens and animated badge notifications
Badge-linked challenges driving engagement at company scale

splashSections.title: Context
splashSections.body: Iris is Egis Group's internal AI assistant. It gives 18,000 employees across 70 countries a single conversational surface for their day-to-day work — drafting, summarising, searching internal knowledge — with an interface that reshapes itself around each use case instead of forcing one generic chat box on everyone.

splashSections.title: Problem
splashSections.body: A general-purpose chatbot doesn't survive contact with a large enterprise. People needed domain-specific entry points, safe handling of confidential documents, and answers that stream fast enough to feel live — inside a product non-technical staff would actually open a second time.
bullets: Adoption had to be pulled, not mandated — the UI needed to earn repeat use
Confidential content meant no shortcuts on document handling and permissions
Perceived latency mattered as much as raw model speed

splashSections.title: Role
splashSections.body: Frontend UI/UX developer in a team of 16, owning the entire interface end-to-end and leading the chat module in particular — from interaction design through to shipped React components.
bullets: Scope: full frontend, with the chat experience as primary ownership
Stack: React, TypeScript, Redux, TanStack Query / Router / Virtualizer, React Aria, Sass, CSS Modules, Vite, Vitest, Docker, GitLab
Backend touchpoints in Django / Python for the endpoints feeding the UI

splashSections.title: Build
splashSections.body: Shipped the core conversational experience and the systems that keep people coming back.
bullets: Real-time token streaming with an interface that adapts per use case
Flows: type "@" in the composer to trigger pre-configured, parameterised prompts
Multi-format handling in one thread — text, images, code, documents
Gamification layer: badge challenges, a company-wide leaderboard, an XP profile
Logo-based custom loading screens and animated badge notifications

splashSections.title: Decisions
splashSections.body: The choices that shaped how the frontend scales and evolves.
bullets: Virtualised the message list so long conversations stay smooth instead of degrading as they grow
Kept server state in TanStack Query and only genuinely global UI state in Redux, avoiding a monolithic store
Built Flows as data-driven config, so new teams onboard without a frontend release
Treated streaming as a first-class UI state — skeletons, partial render, cancellation — not an afterthought

splashSections.title: Impact
splashSections.body: 5,000 daily active users on an 18,000-employee deployment across 70 countries.
bullets: Winner, FCI Awards (large-enterprise category) — "Étincelle d'Or"
Gamification measurably lifted repeat engagement at company scale

memory.name: Memory
memory.description: A personal product I designed and built end-to-end — from the concept and interface design down to the component implementation.
highlights: Concept, interface design and implementation, done solo
A playground for frontend architecture and animation

splashSections.title: Context
splashSections.body: Memory is an internal tool that centralises the group's engineering projects — a single place where any engineer can find company project data, versioned over time, instead of hunting across scattered systems. Designed and built end-to-end as a personal product: concept, interface, components.

splashSections.title: Problem
splashSections.body: The value of the tool scales with how much data it holds — which is also what threatens to break it. None of that volume is allowed to make scrolling stutter or search feel slow, and the UI has to stay legible enough that engineers trust it as the source of truth.
bullets: Multi-thousand-row tables that still need instant filter, sort and search
Project versioning without drowning the UI in history
One person owning design and implementation — it had to stay simple to maintain solo

splashSections.title: Role
splashSections.body: Solo full-stack developer: concept and interface design through to frontend components and the backend integration behind them.
bullets: Scope: end-to-end — design system, components, data layer
Stack: React, TypeScript, TanStack Query / Router, React Aria, CSS Modules, Django / Python, Vitest, Playwright, Vite, Husky, GitLab
Doubled as a playground for frontend architecture and animation

splashSections.title: Build
splashSections.body: A focused tool built around one job: finding project data fast.
bullets: Virtualised data tables handling thousands of rows with client-side filter, sort and search
Project version history surfaced without cluttering the primary view
A strong, user-centric design system driving every component
Animation and micro-interaction treated as part of the core experience, not decoration

splashSections.title: Decisions
splashSections.body: Trade-offs made to keep a solo-maintained codebase fast and coherent.
bullets: Row virtualisation over pagination, so exploration stays fluid and context isn't lost between pages
A tight design-system contract up front, which kept the codebase consistent as it grew
Playwright end-to-end coverage on the flows that matter, to ship confidently without a QA team
Django backend kept deliberately thin — a clean data API, logic pushed where it's cheapest to change

splashSections.title: Impact
splashSections.body: Deployed alongside Iris, giving engineers company project data in one place — a major time and organisation gain.
bullets: Became the default entry point for engineering project data
Proving ground for architecture and animation patterns reused on other work

sustain.name: SustainEcho
sustain.description: A platform for greener building construction. Shipped components and systems end-to-end with a strong focus on user-centric design.
highlights: Dashboard, stepper and data table built from scratch
Filtering, search and sorting across large datasets
Design system in Figma + a full visual identity redesign

splashSections.title: Context
splashSections.body: SustainEcho is a carbon-optimisation platform for the construction industry — a B2B product that helps construction firms swap in lower-carbon materials and get carbon assessments on their builds. The work: lead and fully redesign the interface, and build a design system to carry it.

splashSections.title: Problem
splashSections.body: Joining a project already in flight, in a fast startup, with no prior professional experience. The interface needed a redesign and a system to make it coherent, while large datasets had to stay searchable and sortable without a heavy frontend.
bullets: An in-progress codebase and product to get up to speed on quickly
No design system: the UI was drifting as features landed
Large material and assessment datasets needing fast filter, search and sort

splashSections.title: Role
splashSections.body: Frontend UI/UX developer in a team of around ten, during my final year at Epitech. Led the interface redesign, built the design system, and developed components from scratch.
bullets: Scope: interface redesign, design system, core components, visual identity
Stack: React, JavaScript, Redux, Ant Design, Sass, Django / Python, React Testing Library, Jest, Cypress, Vite, Rollup, Docker, GitHub
Design system built in Figma alongside a full visual-identity refresh

splashSections.title: Build
splashSections.body: Rebuilt the interface on a component library the whole product could share.
bullets: Dashboard, multi-step stepper and data table built from scratch
Filtering, search and sorting across large datasets
A Figma design system plus a complete visual-identity redesign
Reusable component library aligning the product on one language

splashSections.title: Decisions
splashSections.body: Choices that let a small team move fast without the UI fragmenting.
bullets: Built on Ant Design but wrapped it behind project components, so the design system — not the vendor — set the visual rules
Prioritised the stepper and data table first: the highest-friction flows for users entering build data
Locked the visual identity early in Figma so redesign and feature work didn't diverge
Layered testing — RTL, Jest, Cypress — to move fast on a small team without regressions

splashSections.title: Impact
splashSections.body: Acquired by Egis Group after one year, and now commercialised under the name Emersus.
bullets: First large-scale project: from no professional experience to owning the interface and design system
The redesigned system carried through to the commercial product

education.description: Including a fourth year abroad at UQAC (Université du Québec à Chicoutimi), Quebec — coursework in Java, AI and English.
